inputs.story: A series of competitive rowers recently raced to see who among them could be the first to cross the Pacific westwards, from California to Japan. Using only the clues that follow, match each racer to his or her rowing time (in days), and determine their start and end points. Remember, as with all grid-based logic puzzles, no option in any category will ever be used more than once.
inputs.constraints:
1. The athlete who traveled for 195 days started from Pescadero.
2. Of Dana and the athlete who traveled for 184 days, one started from Cayucos and the other started from Bodega Bay .
3. Hilda finished in 217 days .
4. Walter finished 11 days before the athlete who started from Cayucos.

durations: 184 days; 195 days; 206 days; 217 days.
rowers: Antonio; Dana; Hilda; Walter.
start points: Bodega Bay; Cayucos; Pescadero; Pismo Beach.
inputs.solution:

184 days	Antonio	Bodega Bay
195 days	Walter	Pescadero
206 days	Dana	Cayucos
217 days	Hilda	Pismo Beach

Consider N-Queens Puzzle on a chessboard of size 8x8. The goal is to assign 8 queens on the chessboard so that no two queens can share the same row, column, or diagonal.

index_of_column: 1; 2; 3; 4; 5; 6; 7; 8.
